'''Benjamin Louis Handlogten''' (born November 16, 1973) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) and other leagues. ==Early life and education== Handlogten, who was born in [[Grand Rapids, Michigan]], graduated from [[South Christian High School]] of Grand Rapids and attended [[Western Michigan University]] in [[Kalamazoo, Michigan]]. ==Professional career== Handlogten grew up as a [[Detroit Pistons]] fan during the "[[Detroit Pistons#1979-1994: The Bad Boys era|Bad Boys]]" era of the team.{{cite web|title=Ben Handlogten Interview|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/handlogten-interview-101605.shtml|work=InsideHoops.com|accessdate=March 2, 2013|date=October 16, 2005}} Not selected in the [[1996 NBA draft]], Handlogten signed with the Pistons as a free agent on September 18, 1996, but was cut before the regular season.{{cite web|title=Ben Handlogten|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Ben_Handlogten/Summary/1142|work=RealGM|accessdate=March 2, 2013}} He entered professional basketball in 1996 with the [[Grand Rapids Hoops]] of the [[Continental Basketball Association]]. For the 1997–98 season, Handlogten played for [[Oyak Renault]] of the [[Turkish Basketball League]] (TBL) and averaged 17.6 points, 10.4 rebounds, and 1.4 blocks. In 1998, Handlogten signed with [[Niigata Albirex BB|Daiwa]] of the Japanese [[bj league]] and had an average 16.6 points, 11.8 rebounds, and 1.5 blocks.{{cite web|title=Ben Handlogten biography|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/ben_handlogten/bio.html|publisher=NBA|accessdate=March 1, 2013|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130515150459/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/ben_handlogten/bio.html|archivedate=May 15, 2013}} After his one season with Daiwa, Handlogten played two more seasons in the TBL: with [[Galatasaray Medical Park (men's basketball)|Galatasaray]] in 1999–2000 and [[Ülkerspor]] in 2000–01. Handlogten averaged 17.4 points and 8.4 rebounds in the 2001–02 season with [[Virtus Roma]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]]. In the 2002–03 season, Handlogten played for [[Makedonikos B.C.]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and was the league's top rebounder that season with 12.8 per game. With Makedonikos, Handlogten scored an average of 16.8 points per game and also had 1.4 assists and 1.1 blocks per game. He signed as an undrafted free agent with the [[Utah Jazz]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) on September 30, 2003.{{cite web|title=Ben Handlogten|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/handlbe01.html|publisher=basketball-reference.com|accessdate=March 2, 2013}} Handlogten played 17 games and averaged 4.0 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 0.4 assists before a season-ending [[ACL injury]] on December 26, 2003. Handlogten scored a career-high 13 points on December 12{{cite web|last=Hamilton|first=Linda|title=Handlogten happy to hit road|url=http://www.deseretnews.com/article/570036796/Handlogten-happy-to-hit-road.html?pg=all|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304000535/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/570036796/Handlogten-happy-to-hit-road.html?pg=all|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 4, 2016|work=Deseret News|access-date=March 2, 2013|date=December 15, 2003}} and grabbed a season-high 9 rebounds two days later, December 14. On February 19, 2004, the Jazz traded Handlogten and [[Keon Clark]] to the [[Phoenix Suns]] for [[Tom Gugliotta]] and future draft picks; the Suns waived Handlogten the following day. Following two ten-day contracts, Handlogten signed a contract for the rest of the season with the Utah Jazz on March 29, 2005. He averaged 4.5 points, 3.1 rebounds, and 0.6 assists in 21 games (5 starts). On April 1, Handlogten scored a season-high 12 points and grabbed a season- and career-high 11 rebounds. The [[New Jersey Nets]] waived Handlogten on November 8, 2005, after Handlogten signed on October 4. Handlogten then signed with [[Ulsan Mobis Phoebus]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]] the following week. On February 19, 2006, he agreed to join [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|Winterthur FC Barcelona]] of [[Liga ACB]] for the rest of the season.{{cite web|title=El Winterthur FC Barcelona ficha a Ben Handlogten hasta final de campaña|url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=29832|publisher=Liga ACB|accessdate=March 2, 2013|language=Spanish|date=February 20, 2006}} However, the team delayed the signing pending medical examinations.http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=29958 {{Dead link|date=February 2022}} In March 2006, he was cut by the team.[http://www.24sec.net/article.asp?index=3178 Barcelona cuts Handlogten] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071028051144/http://www.24sec.net/article.asp?index=3178 |date=October 28, 2007 }} ==Post-playing career== After his basketball career, Handlogten became owner of a real estate/construction company in [[Charlotte, North Carolina]].{{cite web|last=Buckley|first=Tim|title=Utah Jazz notebook: Injuries mounting for Jazz|url=http://www.deseretnews.com/article/705348036/Utah-Jazz-notebook-Injuries-mounting-for-Jazz.html?pg=all|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131216100550/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/705348036/Utah-Jazz-notebook-Injuries-mounting-for-Jazz.html?pg=all|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 16, 2013|work=Deseret News|accessdate=March 1, 2013|date=November 30, 2009}} Joining the school as an assistant coach in 2008, Handlogten became head boys' basketball coach at [[SouthLake Christian Academy]] of [[Huntersville, North Carolina]].{{cite web|last=Tovar|first=Sergio|title=Former NBA center takes Eagles' reigns|url=http://www.charlotteobserver.com/2010/06/23/1509668/former-nba-center-takes-eagles.html|work=Lake Norman News|accessdate=March 2, 2013|date=June 23,
